description:
Open an installed app, or confirm the running renderer (Chromium).
Use when starting any app; prefer this over tapping home-screen / launcher icons. Also prepares the native-devtools injection before the app starts (iOS and Apple TV).
Returns { launched, bundleId, note?, networkCapture? }. Fails if the app is not installed on the target device (iOS / Android). On a physical iPhone this registers the app every other tool acts on; com.apple.springboard and com.apple.Spotlight register without launching. note warns when runner signing is not ready. networkCapture (Android) says whether native network capture followed the launch.
For Chromium, the app is already running behind a CDP port; this call simply refreshes the cached viewport and acknowledges the bundleId tag. To change the visible route, use `open-url`.

Common iOS bundle ids: com.apple.MobileSMS, com.apple.mobilesafari, com.apple.Preferences, com.apple.Maps, com.apple.mobileslideshow (Photos), com.apple.MobileAddressBook
Common Android packages: com.android.settings, com.android.chrome, com.google.android.apps.maps, com.google.android.gm, com.android.vending, com.google.android.dialer, com.google.android.apps.messaging

activity.description: Android-only: fully-qualified Activity name (e.g. `.MainActivity` or `com.example/com.example.MainActivity`). If omitted, the app's default launcher activity is used.

bundleId.description: App identifier. iOS: bundle id. Android: package name from build.gradle `applicationId`. Vega (Fire TV): the interactive component app id from manifest.toml (e.g. com.example.app.main). Chromium: any tag matching the pattern.

launchArgs.description: Apple simulators and physical iPhones: arguments passed to the app process at launch, e.g. `["-FeatureFlag", "YES"]` to override UserDefaults. A running app is relaunched to apply them. The call fails, launching nothing, if terminating it does not finish within 15s on a local iOS simulator, or fails for a reason other than the app not running on a remote one.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, or Chromium id).
